'''''Youngia japonica''''', commonly called '''Oriental false hawksbeard''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=YOJA|taxon=Youngia japonica|access-date=8 January 2018}}</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Asteraceae]]. Native to eastern [[Asia]], it is now found as a weed nearly worldwide.

==Genomics==
A chromosome-level [[Sequence assembly|genome assembly]] of ''Youngia japonica'' was published in 2026. The [[genome]] is approximately 1.14 Gb in size, with the assembled sequences anchored onto 8 [[chromosomes|pseudo-chromosomes]]. The assembly has a BUSCO completeness of 95.4%, and 35,827 [[protein-coding genes]] were predicted.<ref name="Peng2026">{{cite journal | last1 = Peng | first1 = Yulan | last2 = Pu | first2 = Xuemei | last3 = Cao | first3 = Tingying | last4 = Ju | first4 = Wenbing | last5 = Bian | first5 = Fuhua | last6 = Wang | first6 = Yanjie | title = Chromosome-level genome assembly of ''Youngia japonica'' reveals evolutionary dynamics underlying adaptation in a synanthropic Asteraceae species | journal = BMC Plant Biology | date = 18 April 2026 | doi = 10.1186/s12870-026-08657-w | doi-access = free| pmid = 42001007 }}</ref>

==Description==
It is an annual that produces yellow flowers. In [[Tropics|tropical]] areas, it can bloom year round, while in temperate areas it blooms in late spring and early summer.<ref name=fna/> Plants are variable in height, ranging from {{convert|10|to|150|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} depending on growing conditions. Stems are usually solitary and erect. Basal leaves are large and pinnately divided. Its fruits are wind dispersed.<ref name=foc/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Youngia japonica'' is native to eastern Asia in [[China]] and [[Japan]].<ref name=foc>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200024672 Flora of China, ''Youngia japonica'']</ref><ref name="Ohwi">{{cite book |last=Ohwi |first=Jisaburo |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/bibliography/43786 |title=Flora of Japan |publisher=[[Smithsonian Institution]] |year=1965 |location=Washington |pages=930 |language=en |doi=10.5962/bhl.title.43786 |lccn=65062683 |oclc=182709297}}</ref> However, it has been spread far from its initial range, and is now found as a non-native species nearly worldwide. It is present in Africa, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America.<ref name=fna>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200024672 Flora of North America, ''Youngia japonica'']</ref> In the [[United States]], it is spreading rapidly, although it is largely restricted to areas in the Southeast.<ref name=Weakley>{{cite web |url=http://www.herbarium.unc.edu/flora.htm |title=Flora of the Southern and Mid-Atlantic States |author=Alan Weakley |date=2015 |access-date=2018-01-08 |archive-date=2018-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006082209/http://herbarium.unc.edu/flora.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{BONAP|ref|genus=Youngia|species=japonica|access-date=8 January 2018}}</ref> It grows well in response to human disturbance, and is found in areas such as roadsides, cultivated fields and in lawns.<ref name=fna/> In China, it is found in a variety of natural and disturbed habitats.<ref name=foc/> It is known to penetrate into intact natural communities as an invasive species in the United States.<ref name=Weakley/>

==Taxonomy==
Three subspecies are recognized. They are:<ref name=foc/>
*''Youngia japonica'' subsp. ''elstonii'' - With many stem leaves. Not known to be weedy. 
*''Youngia japonica'' subsp. ''japonica'' - With few to no stem leaves. A weed found nearly worldwide.
*''Youngia japonica'' subsp. ''longiflora'' - Has larger flowers. Not known to be weedy. This is considered the most distinct subspecies.

It has been reported to form intergeneric [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] with ''[[Lapsanastrum humile]]'' in Japan.<ref name=Ohwi/>
